source: CHIJ St. Theresa's Convent Preliminary Examination 2022 Mathematics Paper 1 & Paper 2 (4048/01 & 4048/02)
notes: Word-only items only. Diagram, graph, construction, sketch and scale-drawing questions omitted. Answers from the separate marking-scheme PDFs; notation cleaned for bulk import. Spot-check Q4 (P1 currency) and Q10a (indices) against the papers before seeding.

questions.prompt: Simplify 2(5a + 3b) - 3(a - 2b).

Factorise completely:

2x^2 + 5x - 3.

Factorise completely:

3ax + 6ay - x - 2y.

If Abigail sells a bicycle for $270, she would make a loss of 25%.

How much must she sell the bicycle for to make a profit of 40%?
questions.explanation:
75% of cost price = $270, so cost price = $360.
140% of cost price = 1.4 x 360 = $504.

questions.prompt:
Cerra changed S$500 to US dollars in January at a rate of S$1 = USD 0.753.
In October, she changed the US dollars back to Singapore dollars at a rate of S$1 = USD 0.722.

Find the difference in the amount of Singapore dollars she received. Give your answer correct to the nearest cent.
questions.explanation:
USD received = 500 x 0.753 = USD 376.50.
S$ on return = 376.50 / 0.722 = S$521.47 (nearest cent).
Difference = 521.47 - 500 = S$21.47.

questions.prompt:
Solve the equation

x/3 - (2x - 5)/2 = 1.
Given that q = 25 - 2p^2, find q when p = -3.
Given that q = 25 - 2p^2, rearrange the formula to make p the subject.
Given that x - y = 7 and xy = 18, find the values of x^2 - y^2.

4^k = 1/4^9 + 1/4^9 + 1/4^9 + 1/4^9.

Without the use of a calculator, find the value of k.

The values of seven numbers are (x - 3), (x + 3), (x - 4), (x + 7), (x + 4), (x - 3), (x + 2).

Find the value of x if the sum of the mode and the median of the numbers is 17.

A map has a scale of 1 : 50 000.

The distance from Jurong to Changi is 26 km. Calculate the distance, in centimetres, between Jurong and Changi on the map.
questions.explanation:
1 cm on map = 50 000 cm = 0.5 km.
26 km is represented by 26 / 0.5 = 52 cm.

questions.prompt:
A map has a scale of 1 : 50 000.

The East Coast Park has an area of 1.85 km^2. Calculate the area, in square centimetres, of East Coast Park on the map.
questions.explanation:
1 cm on the map represents 0.5 km, so 1 cm^2 represents 0.25 km^2.
Area on map = 1.85 / 0.25 = 7.4 cm^2.
Marking scheme gives 74 cm^2 — spot-check the paper scale wording before seeding.

questions.prompt:
The graph of y = (x + a)(2 - x) cuts the y-axis at R(0, 14).

Find the value of a.
For y = (x + 7)(2 - x), state the equation of the line of symmetry.
questions.explanation:
Roots are x = -7 and x = 2.
Axis of symmetry: x = (-7 + 2)/2 = -2.5.

questions.prompt: Express x^2 - 6x + 11 in the form (x - h)^2 + k.
Find the prime factors of 35 000, giving your answer in index form.

P = a^4 x b^3 x 7 and Q = a x b^c x 7. The LCM of P and Q is 35 000 = 2^3 x 5^3 x 7.

Write down the values of a, b and c.
questions.explanation: From LCM: a^4 supplies 2^3 so a = 2; b^3 supplies 5^3 so b = 5; c + 1 = 4 so c = 3.

questions.prompt:
P = 2^4 x 5^3 x 7 and Q = 2 x 5^3 x 7.

Find the highest common factor (HCF) of P and Q.

Eunice bought a 3-Room HDB apartment for $120 000. She paid 15% downpayment and took a loan on the outstanding balance for 10 years at r% per annum compounded annually. Her monthly instalment was $1270.

Calculate r.

In a sequence, the same number is subtracted each time to obtain the next term. The first five terms are 17, p, q, r, 7.

Find the value of r.
questions.explanation:
Common difference d = -6 (from T_n = -6n + 23).
Fourth term r = 17 + 3(-6) = -1.

questions.prompt:
An arithmetic sequence has first term 17 and common difference -6.

Find an expression, in terms of n, for the nth term.

The nth term of a sequence is -6n + 23.

Explain why -345 is not a term of this sequence.
questions.model_answer: -345 is not a term because n would not be an integer.
questions.explanation:
-6n + 23 = -345 gives -6n = -368, so n = 61.33...
Since n must be a positive integer, -345 is not a term.

questions.prompt: A box contains 5 red marbles and 3 green marbles. One marble is chosen at random. Find the probability of obtaining a green marble.
A fair 6-sided die is rolled. Find the probability of obtaining a prime number.
questions.explanation:
Prime outcomes: 2, 3, 5 — three out of six.
P = 3/6 = 1/2.

questions.prompt: A number is selected at random from {3, 5, 7, 9}. Find the probability of obtaining an even number.
questions.explanation: None of the numbers is even, so P(even) = 0.

questions.prompt: Express y/(3y - 5)^2 + 2/(5 - 3y) as a single fraction in its simplest form.

Solve the inequality

(3x - 2)/4 <= (4 + 5x)/3.

Solve the simultaneous equations:

4x - 3y = 5
6x + 5y = -2

A bag contains 10 red balls and 8 green balls. Anna takes two balls at random without replacement. She claims P(one red and one green) = 2/9.

Explain why she is wrong and find the correct probability.
questions.model_answer: 80/153 (she ignored that the draws are without replacement)

questions.prompt:
A bag has 10 red and 8 green balls. n red balls are removed. Two balls are then drawn without replacement. P(both green) = 4/13.

Show that n^2 - 35n + 124 = 0.
questions.explanation:
P(both green) = [8/(18-n)] x [7/(17-n)] = 4/13.
Cross-multiply and expand to get n^2 - 35n + 124 = 0.

questions.prompt: When solving n^2 - 35n + 124 = 0 for the number of red balls removed from a bag that originally had only 10 red balls, explain why one solution must be rejected.
questions.model_answer: n = 31 is impossible because there are only 10 red balls.
questions.explanation: Removing 31 red balls would leave a negative number of red balls, so n = 31 is rejected. n = 4 is valid.

questions.prompt: A is the point (-1, 3) and B is the point (7, 9). Find the length of AB.

ABCD is a trapezium with AB parallel to CD. A(-1, 3), B(7, 9) and AD = (1, -7).

Find the equation of the line CD.

A(-1, 3), B(7, 9). Point X lies on AB such that area(triangle AXD) : area(triangle BXD) = 1 : 3.

Find AX.
questions.explanation:
Equal heights from D to AB, so AX : XB = 1 : 3.
AX = 1/4 x AB = 1/4 x 10 = 2.5 units.

questions.prompt:
O is the origin. A(-1, 3), B(7, 9) and X divides AB in the ratio AX : XB = 1 : 3.

Find the position vector of X.

Coffee prices ($): Cafe X — Americano 5.20, Latte 6.60, Mocha 7.30. Cafe Y — Americano 5.50, Latte 6.40, Mocha 7.40.

Belinda buys 2 Americano, 4 Latte, 3 Mocha. Carol buys 5 Latte, 4 Mocha.

Represent their purchases in a 3 x 2 matrix Q (rows: drink types A, L, M; columns: Belinda, Carol).
questions.explanation: Row 1 = Americano counts, row 2 = Latte, row 3 = Mocha for Belinda and Carol.

questions.prompt:
R = PQ where row 1 is Cafe X and row 2 is Cafe Y, and columns are Belinda and Carol.

State what each element of R represents.
questions.model_answer: Each element is the total cost of the drinks ordered by Belinda or Carol at that cafe.
questions.explanation: R[1,1] = Belinda's bill at Cafe X; R[1,2] = Carol's bill at Cafe X; R[2,1] and R[2,2] are the same for Cafe Y.

questions.prompt:
Belinda and Carol each buy from the cheaper cafe in February (Belinda: 2A, 4L, 3M; Carol: 5L, 4M). In July they buy the same from the same cafes. Prices change: Americano +10%, Latte +15%, Mocha -5% (both cafes).

Calculate the percentage change in the combined total spent (February + July vs February alone doubled).
questions.explanation:
February: Belinda at Cafe X ($58.70), Carol at Cafe Y ($61.60) — total $120.30.
July with +10% A, +15% L, -5% M at same cafes: total ≈ $127.53.
Combined Feb + July = $247.83.
Percentage increase on Feb-only baseline (2 x $120.30): (247.83 - 240.60)/240.60 x 100% ≈ 6.01%.

questions.prompt:
40 students: time on social media (hours) — <10: p, 10-20: 11, 20-30: 10, 30-40: q, 40-50: 3. Upper quartile = 30 hours.

Show that p = 9 and find q.
questions.explanation:
75% of 40 = 30 students at most 30 hours.
p + 11 + 10 = 30, so p = 9.
q = 40 - 30 - 3 = 7.

questions.prompt:
Grouped data (midpoints 5, 15, 25, 35, 45) with frequencies 9, 11, 10, 7, 3.

Estimate the mean number of hours spent on social media.
For the grouped data with frequencies 9, 11, 10, 7, 3 and midpoints 5, 15, 25, 35, 45, estimate the standard deviation.
questions.explanation: Use calculator statistics on grouped data: SD ≈ 12.2 hours (3 s.f.).

questions.prompt:
Exchange rates (SGD to KRW): lowest 1 SGD = 908.724 KRW, highest 1 SGD = 939.752 KRW.

A family of 4 needs PCR tests in South Korea at 70 000 won each. Find the difference between the greatest and least possible cost in Singapore dollars, correct to the nearest ten cents.
questions.explanation:
Max cost (lowest rate) = 4 x 70000/908.724 ≈ S$308.12.
Min cost (highest rate) = 4 x 70000/939.752 ≈ S$297.95.
Difference ≈ S$10.17 ≈ S$10.20.
